headline: Nearly half of new Singapore private bank accounts opened within a month
body: Nearly half of new accounts at Private Banking Industry Group (PBIG) member banks were opened within a month between June and August 2026, according to the group. PBIG aims to bring the median account opening time to within one month by the end of 2026. Banks’ efforts include using AI and digital tools, adopting risk-proportionate approaches to Source of Wealth due diligence and removing excessive processes.
note: A regulator co-chairing a bank group that credits AI and digital tools for faster onboarding shows Singapore will let private banks automate parts of client due diligence, a trade other wealth hubs competing for the same assets are watched against too.

evidence.text: Nearly half of new accounts at Private Banking Industry Group (PBIG) member banks were opened within a month between June and August 2026, according to the group.
Most member banks have reduced their account opening times since the end of 2025.
PBIG aims to bring the median account opening time to within one month by the end of 2026.
Banks’ efforts include using AI and digital tools, adopting risk-proportionate approaches to Source of Wealth due diligence and removing excessive processes.
Gillian Tan, Assistant Managing Director (Development and International) of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and co-chair of PBIG, said,

“The progress made in shortening account opening times is a strong signal of the industry’s commitment to meet clients’ needs and strengthen Singapore’s competitiveness as a trusted and efficient wealth management centre.
